newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia's T-bill rate cut by a percent at auction.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's T-bill rate cut by a percent at auction.

text.p: The coupon rate on Tunisian treasury bills dropped by one percent at this week's Treasury auction as a result of the 1.0-point cut on the average money marker rate last week.
The Treasury said it sold 14 million dinars of three-year notes payable in equal annual tranches at a coupon rate of 8.0625 percent at its weekly auction dated Tuesday November 19.
The last rate was 9.0625 percent for similar maturity at the auction dated November 5.
The weekly auction was skipped for Tuesday, November 12 as it coincided with the Central Bank's cut of the average money market interest rate by one point to 7.8125 from 8.8125 percent.

Banks this week bid for 103 million dinars. They offered to purchase three-year notes payable in equal annual tranches at 8.0625 percent for an amount of 14 million dinars, at 8,2500 percent for an amount of three million dinars and 9,000 percent for an amount of six million dinars.

They also offered 8.500 percent for the purchase of five-year notes payable in equal annual tranches, 8.5000 percent for an amount of 75 million dinars and 9,2500 percent for an amount of five million dinars.
The treasury sold only three-year paper and repaid maturing paper worth 42.6 million dinars. ($=0.98 dinar)
